name: Diabetic Autonomic Neuropathy

prevalence.estimate: 20-73% of diabetic patients depending on diagnostic criteria and disease duration
prevalence.range: Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy in 20% of unselected diabetics, up to 65% in long-standing disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Toronto Consensus Panel on Diabetic Neuropathy / ADA Guidelines

criteria.description: Established diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (Type 1 or Type 2)
Abnormal heart rate variability testing (reduced R-R interval variation on deep breathing, Valsalva ratio, or 30:15 ratio on standing)
Orthostatic hypotension (>=20/10 mmHg drop on standing)
Symptoms of autonomic dysfunction in at least one organ system (cardiovascular, GI, genitourinary, sudomotor)
Exclusion of other causes of autonomic neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diabetes mellitus plus at least one abnormal cardiovascular autonomic reflex test; two or more abnormal tests recommended for definite CAN
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Screening recommended at diagnosis in Type 2 DM and 5 years after diagnosis in Type 1 DM. CAN is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular mortality.

common.notes: Due to vagal denervation; heart rate may become fixed later

occasional.notes: Loss of sympathetic warning symptoms during hypoglycemia

occasional.symptomName: Anhidrosis of feet with compensatory truncal sweating

occasional.notes: Absence of angina during ischemic events due to afferent denervation

laboratory: Fasting glucose or OGTT confirming diabetes
imaging: Cardiac MIBG: may show reduced uptake (postganglionic denervation)
genetic: No specific genetic markers for DAN
Genetic risk factors for diabetes (HLA for T1DM, TCF7L2 for T2DM)
other: Cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests (Ewing battery): abnormal HR variability on deep breathing, abnormal Valsalva ratio, abnormal 30:15 ratio
Sudoscan: reduced electrochemical skin conductance in feet

distinguishingFeatures: PAF has more severe and isolated autonomic failure
AAG has subacute onset and may have gAChR antibodies
DAN is gradual over years with long-standing diabetes
Amyloidosis has multisystem deposits and characteristic biopsy findings
Amyloid neuropathy may have more severe small fiber involvement

redFlags: Silent myocardial ischemia (cardiac events without chest pain)
Hypoglycemia unawareness (risk of severe hypoglycemic events)
references: Pop-Busui R, et al. Diabetic neuropathy: a position statement by the American Diabetes Association. Diabetes Care. 2017;40(1):136-154.
Vinik AI, et al. Diabetic autonomic neuropathy. Diabetes Care. 2003;26(5):1553-1579.
Spallone V, et al. Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy in diabetes: clinical impact, assessment, diagnosis, and management. Diabetes Metab Res Rev. 2011;27(7):639-653.
